name: Septoplasty

lead: Septoplasty straightens the nasal septum, the wall of cartilage and bone between the nostrils, when it is bent enough to block airflow. The main payoff is easier breathing. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up because people with a crooked septum ask whether it will make the nose look straighter or should be combined with rhinoplasty or jaw surgery.

The surgeon works through the nostrils, repositioning or removing deviated bone and cartilage. Alone it may not straighten a crooked-looking nose, since the external shape is not the goal. A multicentre prospective study and a 2023 BMJ randomised trial found symptom improvement after septoplasty.

paras: It is usually an outpatient operation under local or general anaesthesia, lasting about an hour or less. When people also want the outer nose reshaped, it is performed together with rhinoplasty as septorhinoplasty.

Reported risks include bleeding, septal perforation, septal haematoma, reduced sense of smell, temporary numbness of the front upper teeth, and, less often, a dropped nasal tip or saddle deformity from over-resection. Symptoms can persist or recur in some patients.

chain: Airway opens and nose aligns better
angle.text: Septoplasty straightens the inner septum to open the airway, and people discuss it because the realignment can bring small changes in how the nose sits, such as at the tip. Alone it may not straighten a crooked-looking nose, and it is often combined with rhinoplasty.

lead: Septoplasty is a surgical procedure that straightens a deviated nasal septum, the partition between the two nasal cavities, to relieve obstruction.[1][2] It is also called septal reconstruction or submucous septal resection.[1] It is performed through the nostrils, under local or general anaesthesia, and most operations take about an hour or less according to Wikipedia.[1]

Its main indications are nasal obstruction, recurrent nosebleeds from a septal spur, and associated rhinitis or sinus problems.[1] A multicentre prospective study of adults with septal deviation and symptomatic obstruction, the NOSE study, found improved disease-specific quality of life after septoplasty.[3] A 2023 randomised trial published in the BMJ found greater improvement in symptoms at six months after septoplasty than with nasal sprays alone.[1]

Septoplasty is distinct from rhinoplasty, which reshapes the external nose, although the two are often performed together as septorhinoplasty.[1][2] In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed mainly as a breathing operation that some users ask about in relation to nose appearance, rhinoplasty and orthognathic surgery.[4][5][6]
infobox: Correct a deviated septum; improve airflow

paras: Septoplasty is used for airway obstruction that causes breathing difficulty, recurrent rhinitis or sinusitis, and for recurrent epistaxis caused by a septal spur.[1] Grokipedia adds that it is typically considered when conservative measures such as nasal sprays and decongestants have not relieved symptoms.[2] The NOSE study enrolled adults with septal deviation and obstruction lasting at least three months in whom medical management had failed.[3]
A deviated septum in some degree is common, and Grokipedia reports estimates that it affects a large proportion of the population, most of them mildly and without symptoms.[2]

The surgeon accesses the septum through the nostrils, incises the lining, and removes or realigns part of the bone or cartilage while preserving enough for structural support. The approach may be endoscopic or open, and splints, sutures or internal grafts may be used.[1] There are no external incisions in the usual approach.[2]

The procedure may be combined with turbinate surgery, sinus surgery, or rhinoplasty. A US survey of ambulatory sinonasal surgery grouped septoplasty and turbinate surgery as one of the most common categories of such operations.[7] A plastic-surgery study examined the relative importance of septal and nasal-valve surgery in correcting airway obstruction in primary and secondary rhinoplasty.[8]

External swelling or bruising is usually minimal. Internal splints are often removed 7 to 10 days after surgery, and tissues generally stabilise over 3 to 6 months, with some shifting possible for over a year.[1]

Wikipedia lists excessive bleeding (about 1% of patients), septal perforation, septal haematoma, reduced smell, temporary numbness of the upper front teeth, a dropped nasal tip, empty nose syndrome, septal abscess, adhesions and saddle nose from over-resection as possible complications. It lists acute infection, untreated diabetes, severe hypertension and bleeding disorders as contraindications.[1] Grokipedia reports that revision surgery may be needed in some patients and that obstruction can recur over years.[2]

Because the cartilaginous septum supports the nasal tip and dorsum, surgery on it can influence nasal structure, and septal cartilage is often harvested for grafting in rhinoplasty.[2][9] A series of surgeons' technique papers, such as a 10-year experience with the tongue-in-groove technique in septorhinoplasty, address combining septal and cosmetic work.[9] A purely functional septoplasty is not intended to change the external shape.[2]

On looksmax.org, users post about scheduling septoplasty for breathing reasons and asking whether surgeons will also adjust the nasal tip during an insurance-covered operation.[4] Other threads ask whether septoplasty alone can straighten a crooked-looking nose, whether to wait for jaw surgery before addressing the nose, and how recovery felt.[5][6] A separate thread discusses turbinate reduction versus other options, with some users warning about empty nose syndrome and others saying turbinate reduction is the only fix for true turbinate obstruction.[10]

The NOSE study, a prospective multicentre observational study, assessed disease-specific quality of life after septoplasty in adults with nasal obstruction and reported improvement.[3] A 2023 BMJ randomised trial reported greater improvement in symptoms and quality of life at six months after septoplasty than with nasal-spray management.[1]

Registered trials include comparisons of conventional versus endoscopic septoplasty,[11][12] a trial of septoplasty with or without inferior turbinate reduction,[13] a study of silastic sheets after septoplasty,[14] and a trial of septoplasty's effect on headache that was recruiting at the time of the registry listing.[15] Results of several of these registrations are not described in the registry entries.

lore.intro: Forum users discuss septoplasty mainly as a covered breathing operation and ask whether it can double as an aesthetic fix or be paired with other facial surgery.[4][5][6]

claims.claim: A functional septoplasty can be used to make small cosmetic changes to the nose, such as the tip.
Septoplasty alone may not straighten a crooked-looking nose, so some wait for or combine rhinoplasty or jaw surgery.
